method: Read each episode title and its available RSS description. Use the historical subject's event date, life dates or a bounded narrative period, never the release date. Official archive summaries supplement missing descriptions for the newer episodes. The c. prefix marks deliberately approximate coverage. A single region denotes the central historical setting, while transregional journeys use Across the world. Mythic events and all-era conversations remain off the timeline.

cautions: These are editorial subject ranges based on catalogue material, not a transcript-level audit of every date mentioned.
Several original catalogue descriptions contain apparent historical typos, including Poltava in 1707 and Saint George in the third century BCE. Those are not used as historical dates.
The King Arthur, Odyssey, Greek myths, Helen of Troy, dragons, Pope Joan and Saint George episodes remain in Myths & mysteries, avoiding false historical dates for the legendary narratives.
Uruk, Alexandria, Viking ritual and long city/dynasty surveys use broad approximate periods. A single precise year would imply unsupported certainty.
Gallipoli is assigned to Europe because its battlefield is on the European peninsula of Turkey; Egypt and the ancient Library of Alexandria are assigned to Africa.
The older official-archive pages could not be fetched through the shell because the public endpoint returned HTTP 403; their RSS descriptions were available and were read.
